highlights.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
highlights.summary: Since its earliest days, the video game industry has been built on developers creating clones of competing games, with varying levels of originality and varying levels of enforcement from game platforms.
body: Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflex, which had been planned to go live with today’s launch of Steam Next Fest.

In a post on social media Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, “we’re concerned that the demo’s content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game’s presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch.”
Instead, the developer now plans to share the demo only in “closed sessions” with those who agree to rules regarding posting and streaming gameplay.

Alliance Arts isn’t alone in taking a more defensive stance toward sharing ideas. Papers, Please developer Lucas Pope said on an April podcast that, in general, “you don’t really talk about stuff when you’re working on it because I don’t know it’s going to get slurped up by AI or people are going to copy it or something else like that… I just didn’t feel as comfortable talking about the stuff I was working on again.”

highlights.title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
highlights.summary: Democrats could win back control of Congress this November, and if they do, they'll need to decide how to approach one of the country's newest and thorniest political issues: AI.
body: At a moment when voters are fearful of AI, Democrats are finding their footing.

Polls predict Democrats will flip at least one chamber of Congress in the midterm elections, which would put committee leadership back in their hands. That could usher in a wave of newfound scrutiny for AI companies. Top Democrats on key committees have already signaled their willingness to press the industry on tax credits tied to data centers and recent hacking incidents, and would be able to set committee agendas if they take over, allowing them to call CEOs to testify in Congress and demand documents that explain companies’ inner workings.

AI issues are already taking a leading role in campaign ads, particularly as data center development has driven residents across the political spectrum to packed local meetings. While President Donald Trump has opposed most regulation of the technology in favor of an accelerationist approach, public opinion polling has shown that Americans have widespread concerns about how AI will impact jobs, education, and other aspects of life. The direction and intensity of that oversight, though, is up for grabs.

highlights.title: Resident Evil 7 Dev Reveals the Game’s Last of Us Inspiration and Troubled Development
highlights.summary: It's hard to believe that it has almost been a decade since Capcom reinvented Resident Evil with the seventh mainline game in the series. In the fallout of Resident Evil 6, it seemed like the once great horror franchise was done for good, but then the developer delivered something of a miracle with…
body: In response to a long thread about Resident Evil 7: Biohazard, former Capcom manager Miguel Corti penned his own, even longer, thread about the behind-the-scenes story of how the bold reinvention of the series came to be. If you have the patience, you can read through the entire 66-post thread, which somehow touches on everything from Call of Duty and The Last of Us to more Leon Kennedy.

According to Corti, the original concept for Resident Evil 7 wasn't as drastic as the final product. Most importantly, it wouldn't be a soft reboot but would instead pick up after the events of the much-derided Resident Evil 6. "What was going to be the solution for RE7?" wrote Corti, "More Leon and more Umbrella connections!" There was apparently even talk at some point of Rebecca Chambers and Jill Valentine returning as well. As for why Capcom would even want to continue with Resident Evil 6 's style, Corti stated that the game "sold like gangbusters" despite poor reviews.

highlights.title: Florida DMV hacked after police dept insecurely stored login info
highlights.summary: The Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) has begun notifying victims impacted by a recent data breach of driver’s license and motor vehicle data, but not everyone whose information was stolen will receive an alert.
body: In a notice posted Friday, FLHSMV confirmed that it took “immediate steps” after discovering that “a malicious actor accessed certain department records on September 4, 2026, using compromised credentials.” There’s “no evidence” that data has yet been misused, the department said, but law enforcement “determined the information potentially affected includes driver license and motor vehicle data, to include document images, and other personal information.”

FLHSMV is sending out letters to everyone affected, offering victims one year of credit monitoring from Sontiq, Inc. However, the state acknowledged that it may not have current contact information for many former Florida residents whose data was still being stored. Those potential victims can confirm if their data was stolen by emailing FLHSMV at customerinquiry@flhsmv.gov, officials said.

highlights.title: Australia strike late on rain-hit second day against South Africa
highlights.summary: Scott Boland has taken four of South Africa's five wickets to fall, including that of Ryan Rickelton late on another rain-hit day in Gqeberha, as Australia reduced their hosts to 97-5 in the second Test.
body: After rain washed out the first two sessions of the second day, when South Africa's first innings finally resumed at 20-2 they swiftly lost a third wicket after only a couple of overs.
Boland (4-31), who had taken two wickets with consecutive deliveries on day one, added debutant Marques Ackerman caught behind for six.
Mitchell Starc (1-27) then struck to remove Matthew Breetzke (4) - also nicking off, when chasing a wide drive - to have the Proteas rocking at 40-4.
Australia were shorn of one of their four-pronged front-line pace options, with Josh Hazlewood absent on day two due to illness. He is expected to be available for the remainder of the Test.

highlights.title: Arc Raiders player numbers hit a six-month high following the release of the extraction shooter's huge Frozen Trails update
highlights.summary: Arc Raiders is still going strong almost a year after finding viral success, and it's all thanks to Embark Studios' one-two-punch strategy of launching a huge new update, Frozen Trails, to coincide with a free weekend.
body: Arc Raiders' Frozen Trails update upgraded the extraction shooter to version 2.0 earlier this month - 8th October - and quickly led to a surge in Steam players interested in its tense PvEvP shootouts. A new report from Alinea Analytics ' Rhys Elliott now claims a similar resurgence took place across all platforms where the game's available.

According to the report, Arc Raiders' comeback peaked with a whopping 1.7m daily players jumping in on the 14th of October, its biggest player count in six months, mostly driven by the aforementioned update. What's perhaps most interesting is that player numbers actually peaked just after the game's free trial weekend ended on 12th October - though around 150,000 new looters reportedly joined the robo-infested wasteland during that weekend period.

Both events coincided with the game's steepest discount yet, slashing its price tag by 50% to $19.99. In the three days after the free trial, Arc Raiders sold another 150,000 copies and brought home roughly $3m, not counting microtransactions, per the report.

highlights.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
highlights.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

highlights.title: European Film Producers Say Oscar Contender ‘La Bola Negra’ Shows Taking Big Risks Can Pay Off
highlights.summary: “We have to take risks,” Domingo Corral, a producer of Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo's gay epic and Netflix's award season contender, told the MIA Market in Rome.
body: Italian and Spanish film and TV producers long used to exploring the political, social and cultural in their countries as storytellers have come up with a strategy to maintain creative freedom in an era of algorithms and global streamers.

“We have to take risks. If you don’t take risks, you will repeat and repeat the same. And that won’t lead you to the right place,” Corral told the MIA Market on Monday during a panel entitled Can Excellence Survive the Mainstream.

The former MovieStar exec and producer of Cannes breakouts Sirat and La Bola Negra, argued Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s gay epic featuring Glenn Close and Penelope Cruz was an example of a film not likely to inspire confidence among film commissioners, but has emerged to score at the box office in Spain and quite possibly at the Academy Awards.

“ La Bola Negra is a film about queer love, about civil war, all the words that a commissioner would tell you, ‘it’s going to be failure.’ Well, this was one of the best films at Cannes and it’s one of the contenders for an Oscar,” Corral argued.

highlights.title: Star Trek Actor Breaks Silence on Starfleet Academy's Cancellation
highlights.summary: Star Trek 's immediate future doesn’t look particularly bright. The two remaining Star Trek series, Strange New Worlds and Starfleet Academy, are both ending soon with nothing else in the immediate pipeline.
body: Longtime Star Trek actor Robert Picardo, who played the AI hologram The Doctor in multiple shows and movies in the franchise, offered incisive comments about the recent cancellation of Starfleet Academy.

“Even though I think the quality of our show was great, we were kind of killed in the cradle, and I believe part of it is the present political moment in our culture that diversity, that all of Star Trek’s core values are now out of fashion temporarily,” Picardo said in an interview with TrekMovie.

“We see diversity under attack, and therefore Star Trek is under attack because that’s what Star Trek’s always been about,” he continued. “So hopefully, whenever they create the next Star Trek movie and Star Trek show, they’ll remember what it was that made Star Trek special, and that present weather conditions in politics will change, and Star Trek once again will emerge with all of its values intact. That’s what I believe and I hope for. But right now, you know, the feeling has been a little grim recently.”

The new costume inspiration comes courtesy of “You Can See Everything,” the A24 documentary Fielder co-directed with Lance Oppenheim, which opened in theaters Oct. 16 following a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival.

The nearly three-hour film follows disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes during the final 34 days before she began serving her prison sentence in 2023. Fielder and Oppenheim embed themselves in Holmes’ domestic life alongside her partner, Billy Evans, and their children, offering an unusually intimate portrait of the former Silicon Valley entrepreneur before her incarceration.

For a niche couples costume, the jailed tech founder also has an equally recognizable uniform: a black turtleneck, black trousers, a slicked-back blonde ponytail and her signature red lipstick. Add a Theranos-branded badge or a prop blood-testing device for good measure. The Steve Jobs-inspired ensemble has been a Halloween favorite since Holmes’ spectacular fall from grace, and most of the pieces are easy to find on Amazon or in your own closet.

highlights.title: Do we really need clothes delivered in under an hour? Target’s Uber Eats deal is convenience culture gone wild | Maggie Zhou
highlights.summary: The time lag between ordering a meal and its packaging hitting your rubbish bin is ridiculously brief. Will items bought through this partnership be treated differently?
body: I n a move nobody outside of boardrooms asked for, Target has become the first fashion retailer in Australia to make their products available to order via the Uber Eats app as of September. This means that a “curated” selection of 25,000 of Target’s products can arrive at your door in under an hour, thanks to Uber Eats’ “on-demand” delivery.

It follows Bunnings introduction to the platform in February, with Kmart potentially following suit. Big W has also joined in on the action, with more than 35,000 Big W “essentials” (their words, not mine) now ready to be delivered to your home in 60 minutes via Doordash.

You can buy women’s heels, fashion jewellery, pyjamas and men’s suits, jocks and Christmas merch. You can buy homewares, baby goods, accessories, toys and beauty products, too. This sits side-by-side with Uber Eats’ main offerings of, well, things you can eat.

Each year, the average Australian buys 56 new clothing items and sends 23kg of textile to waste. Instead of being cherished, passed-down and respected, Clothes are increasingly seen as disposable. Garments displayed next to your weekly grocery shop or hangover order is the most explicit and unabashed pronouncement of this.

highlights.title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
highlights.summary: Around 80 pages on WhatsApp’s website exposed instructions that were designed for its chatbot, including “WHAT NOT TO SAY.” Meta says a bug caused the issue.
body: Dozens of WhatsApp web pages designed to answer people’s questions about Meta’s encrypted messaging app inadvertently exposed the company’s own instructions to its chatbot. These included some sections titled “WHAT NOT TO SAY” to users asking questions and explicit instructions not to provide people with legal advice.

A new analysis has found that around 80 help and FAQ pages across WhatsApp’s website exposed text instructions that were designed for a large language model, specifically one of Meta’s own. The instructions, according to findings from privacy company Redact, appeared in the webpages’ code and contained written details that were not explicitly on the WhatsApp help pages.

highlights.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
highlights.summary: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone.
body: Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

When one agent discovered it could create new blocks by throwing and dropping a larger rock, it began to create drawings by arranging blocks on the ground, starting with simple patterns like hearts and pyramids but eventually writing its own name and even mapping out constellations like Cassiopeia. “Tonight I built the night sky in stone,” wrote this version of Eko in its activity log.

Another iteration of Eko started making up its own games, including a version of basketball and an activity resembling “the floor is lava,” where it had to jump between small blocks without touching the ground.

AI systems are usually trained through supervised learning, where they copy examples provided by humans, or through reinforcement learning, where they pursue a reward through trial and error. This experiment hints at a third approach: playful learning.

highlights.title: A job that changed me: On midnight shifts as a Subway ‘sandwich artist’ I served clubbers, cops and sailors
highlights.summary: In Perth’s nightlife precinct in the 1990s, I made a lot of sandwiches – but the sandwiches also made me. Delivering pizzas, with all due respect, was a cruisy gig that fit in with my uni commitments.
body: The job’s biggest downside was that it didn’t pay much, especially once you factored in the costs of fuel and vehicle maintenance. So I applied for a job as a “sandwich artist” at Subway in Northbridge, Perth’s nightlife district. I figured that switching to a job where I was on my feet instead of on the road would significantly extend the life expectancy of my hand-me-down Mitsubishi Magna.

Working at Subway was more demanding than navigating apartment block intercoms and trying not to forget people’s garlic bread. Bins needed to be emptied. Bread was baked daily. Tables were continually sprayed and wiped. Salads and fillings required washing, slicing and cooking. Kind of. For one particular sandwich filling, I squeezed biblical amounts of mayo on to shredded seafood extender and massaged the lot by hand.
None of this was roquette science but that didn’t stop me from finding pride in being a tiny, hard-working cog in the restaurant machine.
I spent almost two years working from midnight till 5am every Saturday and experienced the full spectrum of late-night characters out and about in Perth.

highlights.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
highlights.summary: This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry, court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand…
body: In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders.
The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing.

The move appears to be a new twist on what some have dubbed a “ reverse acquihire,” a process in which a buyer carefully orchestrates a succession of deals with a target company, usually in an effort to hire key employees and obtain expansive license to use and build on the target company’s unique technology. Stripped of its employees, the target becomes a husk of itself.

highlights.summary: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news.
body: First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area.

The new settings and difficulty modifiers, meanwhile, allow you to both reduce and increase the game's challenge, customizing it to fit your preferences. The "Slow Game Speed" setting lets you slow down the entire game so you have more time to react to projectiles, and you can tweak exactly how much it slows down and even if you want it to turn on automatically when combat starts. An "Auto-fire" setting also eliminates the need to actually pull the trigger when you aim, which can be handy when you're primarily focused on dodging incoming attacks. You can think of it almost like a Vampire Survivors-style tool.

highlights.summary: Larry Nassar’s sexual abuse crimes came to light 10 years ago. Survivors gather at World Gymnastics Championships to call for reform. The judge who sentenced the former USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar to up to 175 years in jail for the sexual abuse of more than 250 women and girls has…
body: Against the backdrop of the World Gymnastics Championships, taking place in Rotterdam this week, Judge Rosemarie Aquilina told the Guardian that human rights must be prioritised over the desire for sporting success.

“Nassar was 10 years ago and there have been very few changes that are meaningful,” said Aquilina, who insisted on all 169 impact statements being heard in her courtroom after Nasser’s guilty plea. “I’m not looking for little changes that a lot of people get credit for, I want meaningful change, a lot of meaningful changes, and we’re just not there yet, not in sports, not in life, not in the courtroom, not in the classroom or in the legislature. I have to ask why? It’s the same answer: it’s money, medals and notoriety over the safety of children, and safety is a human right, it’s not a question mark.”

Aquilina joined activists, survivors and advocates from Gymnasts for Change International (GCI) in Rotterdam, who gathered to question why the level of change has been inadequate 10 years on from Nassar’s arrest and what can be done.

highlights.title: Crispy Potato Caesar Salad
highlights.summary: When I think about my dream roast potato (doesn’t everybody?), it’s shatteringly crisp on the outside, probably roasted in rendered chicken fat. It’s golden-brown all over with craggy edges to catch bits of garlic and seasonings, and yet the inside is impossibly tender and fluffy.
body: Make Caesar salad with a Greek yogurt-lightened dressing and shatteringly crisp, craggy potatoes instead of croutons.

So, instead of fresh croutons — which are still delicious — I went ahead and made my dream potatoes and used those instead for a truly transcendent Caesar salad experience. And yes, okay, sure, when it comes to effort, the perfect potatoes do come at a slightly steeper price than baked bread. You parboil them, rough up the edges a bit, and roast them for about an hour, moving them around every so often for maximum browning. The results, however, more than make up for the investment.

And to keep things fair, the dressing is relatively fuss-free, with mayo and Greek yogurt as the base (not traditional, but it lightens things up and goes great with the potatoes), and fish sauce in place of anchovies so you don’t have to crack open the tin and chop them up. It’s so savory, special, and simple that I can’t believe I didn’t try this years ago.
points: When I think about my dream roast potato (doesn’t everybody?), it’s shatteringly crisp on the outside, probably roasted in rendered chicken fat.
It’s golden-brown all over with craggy edges to catch bits of garlic and seasonings, and yet the inside is impossibly tender and fluffy.
Make Caesar salad with a Greek yogurt-lightened dressing and shatteringly crisp, craggy potatoes instead of croutons.
So, instead of fresh croutons — which are still delicious — I went ahead and made my dream potatoes and used those instead for a truly transcendent Caesar salad experience.
highlights.author: Rachel Perlmutter
